column1: # The SMT session's second half (aws/lab.sh LAB_SUITE=transport LAB_PAIR=a
# LAB_SETS_FILE=<this file>; the matrix's arms are kept): SMT on, on its own
# pair of c7i.4xlarge (Intel, 8 cores x 2 threads). transport-aws-smt-off.tsv
# is the first half, SMT off, with mio-tcp, the baseline this compares with.
# `smt on`: SMT stays on through the isolation reboot, the CPU map isolates
# each core whole (0 1 2,10,3,11,...: housekeeping core 0, IRQ core 1), the
# loop on a core's first thread and its sibling isolated beside it; the
# hostcheck and ergon-io's T10 (SMT on) reported, not refused, and
# fairness.py's smt rule holds each busy thread's sibling to idle or the
# arm's own SQPOLL thread. TCP only: ergon-io's UDP has no uring backend.
#   eio-tcp-sqpoll-sib   ergon-io uring-sqpoll, its SQPOLL thread on the loop
#                        CPU's SMT sibling ({loop_sibling}), no SO_BUSY_POLL
#   mio-tcp-smt          mio as mio-tcp, its loop's sibling idle
#   aa                   eio-tcp-sqpoll-sib again
# Both halves run with the IRQ core capped at C1 (TR_IRQ_IDLE=auto: C1 under
# intel_idle, c7i's driver; every arm, read back per point and recorded in
# transport-settings.tr.env); `irq_idle 1` stops a session whose hosts would
# give anything else before its first point. The first SMT sessions ran uncapped, and the
# c7i diagnosis (transport-aws-c7i-diag.tsv) showed the IRQ core's wake from
# C6 dominating their 10k msg/s points: rerun both halves, never one.
# One stream, ping/pong round trips at 10k, 50k and 200k msg/s, LAB_REPS=3:
# 27 points (LAB_ESTIMATE=1 gives the hours).
smt on
irq_idle 1
# set    pair par host loads              streams netem arms
set smton a   -   ab   10000,50000,200000 1       -     eio-tcp-sqpoll-sib,mio-tcp-smt,aa
